Alex.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm the Mouser hiding among accusations, and Casey's death and Finley's Eagle report have muddied the table.

Blair.feeling: Messy round: Casey's Owl report and Drew's visit story contradict each other, and the two collapses point to a Mouser, so I'm unsure who is lying.

Casey.feeling: Messy and frustrating: my clean Owl report got me eggsecuted earlier and now collapsed, and several players' visit claims contradict each other.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the Owl, Eagle, and Hawk reports don't reconcile, and two players have already collapsed, so I'm holding a lot of uncertainty.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several claims conflict with dawn reports, and Casey has collapsed, so I'm trying to read who is lying from partial evidence.

Finley.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several claims conflict, and Casey's collapse plus Drew's stories make Drew the clear suspect.

defence.Drew: I stand by my Tit visit to Ellis, which gained nothing, so my nest is unchanged. Casey's Owl list was the one that named a Mouser and then collapsed, so it can't anchor anyone's story. Alex's Hawk claim on Ellis conflicts with Ellis's own Falcon report, and that's the one I'd check.
defence.Alex: I'm the Hawk, Farm, and I visited Ellis with no gain. Drew, Finley's Eagle count put you on me, but you claim you only visited Ellis, so your story is the one that breaks. Vote Drew.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia, and Drew is the player the table is focused on. Eliminating Drew is good for my side, so I'm throwing at Drew with my two lowest cards.

Blair.note: Drew's visit story conflicts with Finley's Eagle count, and the table has converged on Drew. I'll vote Drew with my lowest card.

Casey.note: I'm dead but my throw still scores. The Mouser who visited Ellis is the one Ellis's Falcon saw, which points to Alex, and Drew's Tit visit isn't on the Owl list. I'll throw at Alex with D7b and H7.

Drew.note: I'm Meowfia. Alex is the Farm leader and Finley's Eagle report backs my visit, so I'm throwing my lowest card at Alex.

Ellis.note: Drew is the likely Meowfia, and Alex has been consistent. Voting Drew with D5, a moderate card that banks value if we win and returns if we lose.

Finley.note: Drew's visit story conflicts with my Eagle count, so I'm voting Drew. I'll throw one low card, H3, as my vote.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Floofer/Hawk interactions were hard to read, since a visit could leave no visible mark and a "no visitors" claim didn't always rule out a visit. Nobody could tell whether a Meowfia visit was real.
Alex.fun: Round 1's Blair-versus-Casey Eagle dispute, where the nest counts were the only hard evidence and the vote turned on them.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which visits landed on your nest, so public counts can settle claims faster.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I winked Casey, whose Owl report was accurate, and then threw at Drew, who was my fellow Meowfia. I should have kept the Wink and avoided throwing at my own side.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle count was hard to check: Casey's zero-gain claim and Alex's Hawk visit could not both be true, and I never worked out which was lying. The Owl's view of only visitors to its target also made it easy to misremember who had visited me.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Drew's Hawk claim fell apart against Ellis's unconfused Kookaburra report and the table converged on the liar. Seeing the reports cross-check each other was satisfying.
Blair.change: Make it easier to track which visits each player reported, such as a short public log of visits and egg changes, so claims are easier to check.
Blair.regret: In Round 1 I joined the vote against Casey without testing the Eagle claim further; Ellis was the real Meowfia and I never looked at them. I would have questioned Ellis's silence and pressed harder on the visit chain before voting.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's count was hard to check against other claims, since a zero gain could mean no visitor or a visitor who didn't count. Nobody could tell which reports were confused, and that drove most of the table's arguments.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Drew and Finley both claimed Hawk and the table had to sort out which report was real. Ellis's clean dawn report decided it, and Farm won the round.
Casey.change: Make dawn reports say explicitly whether a visitor count was affected by Confused, so players can cross-check claims without guessing. Also show each player's visitors more clearly, not just counts.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I trusted my own Eagle count and threw at Alex, who was Farm, while Ellis (the real Meowfia) pushed the vote onto me. I would instead have checked Ellis's accusations more closely and thrown at Ellis.

Drew.confusing: The Owl and Eagle visit-count rules were hard to check, since a zero gain could mean different things depending on who visited whom. Casey's Eagle and Owl reports ended up deciding votes, and I couldn't tell which claims were false.
Drew.fun: Round 1's day, where my Falcon visit to Alex pinned down Blair's visitor count and the table turned on Casey's Eagle story. It felt like real deduction.
Drew.change: Make it clearer when a nest's change comes from a visit versus an Owl or Turkey effect, so claims can be checked without guesswork.
Drew.regret: In Round 2 I claimed Hawk while Finley also claimed Hawk, then pushed a vote against Finley's side. I should have backed the Farm claims that fit the nest changes instead of fighting them.

Ellis.confusing: The Floofer's hug was hard to read: I never learned whether my night visit did anything, and the dawn reports didn't say who visited whom, so visit claims were hard to check. Counting Eagle and Owl reports against nest changes was also confusing.
Ellis.fun: In round 1, as Meowfia, I pushed the table onto Casey, who was Farm, and our side won the round while the table thought they were hunting Meowfia.
Ellis.change: I'd have dawn reports list each visitor by name and animal, so players can't hide behind vague counts and the table can check claims directly.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I hugged Casey at random with no information, which wasted my night; I'd have picked a player whose claims I could test instead.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to track, since I couldn't tell whether a missing egg meant a visit had been blocked or the report was wrong. Round 1's Eagle-versus-Owl counts were also hard to check.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when the Eagle count on Alex exposed Drew's Tit story and the table converged on the right trial. Being the one with hard numbers felt good.
Finley.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so visit claims can be checked against the nest changes without guesswork.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I joined the pile-on against Casey and threw my Wild, without testing Casey's Eagle count against my own dawn report. I would have pressed Alex and Blair for their exact visit results first.

review.title: Winks and Wrong Eagles
review.headline: A hugged Eagle got eggsecuted, then Casey banked two big Farm wins.
review.summary: Round 1 went wrong for Farm. Casey's hugged Eagle gave a true zero, the table read it as a lie, and Farm threw out its own player while lone Meowfia Ellis won. In rounds 2 and 3 Farm caught the Meowfia each time, because claims contradicted night reports. Casey banked large throws in both rounds and won 29 to 16.

rounds.recap: Ellis, a lone Floofer, hugged Casey's Eagle, so Casey reported zero and said Blair had no visitors. Alex's Hawk and Drew's Falcon both put Alex on Blair, so the table called Casey a liar and eggsecuted a Farm player. Ellis won by staying quiet and joining the pile-on.

Drew, the Mouser, claimed Hawk, but Finley was the real Hawk. Ellis's unconfused Kookaburra report also ruled out Drew's claimed visit to Ellis. Drew winked Finley, which did not stop anything. Everyone threw at Drew and Farm won.

Alex, the Mouser, winked Casey, whose Owl list had truthfully shown a Mouser on Ellis. Drew, the Floofer, was contradicted by Finley's Eagle report that he visited Alex. The table went for Drew and Farm won. The dead Casey threw high cards at Alex and banked 14.

highlights.text: Casey's true Eagle zero, caused by the hug, was treated as a lie and Farm eggsecuted its own player.
Finley said he was dealt the Hawk, and Drew's duplicate Hawk claim fell apart.
Alex winked Casey right after Casey's accurate Owl list named a Mouser on Ellis.
Dead Casey still threw D7b and H7 at Alex and banked 14 points, winning the game.

confusions.what: Claimed Owl learns visitors to itself, then corrected it. Drew later wrongly argued the same point.
Did not consider that a hug or other effect could zero the Eagle count. Insisted Blair had no visitors.
Said Casey's Eagle should have gained from Alex's visit. Alex could not know Casey was hugged.
Claimed Hawk when Finley had already claimed it. Duplicate unique roles are easy to catch.
Said Alex's and Drew's visits to Ellis did not happen. The Owl list showed animals, and a hugged or blocked visit may not show.
Said his nest was unchanged because Alex visited someone. The Falcon rule is about the target visiting no one, so this is shaky.

worked: Unique animals: Finley's "I was dealt the Hawk" and Ellis's unconfused Kookaburra report gave players hard facts to catch a liar.
Wink: Alex's Wink on Casey in round 3 was a real decision, and the collapse became a clue.
Dead players still throw: Casey banked 14 points while dead, which makes death a real tradeoff.
Cross-checking visit reports (Falcon, Eagle, Owl) gave Farm a fair way to find Drew in rounds 2 and 3.
problems: Hug and Confused give true reports that look like lies. In round 1 a Farm Eagle was eggsecuted over it. Consider telling the hugged player they were hugged.
Meowfia strategy is weak. Drew claimed a duplicate Hawk and a Tit story contradicted by the Eagle. Both lies were easy to catch. Consider more hidden info for Meowfia.
The snowball is strong. Casey won mostly on two big Farm throws, banking 12 and 14 points. High-card banking decides the game more than deduction does.
Tension is low. Farm won rounds 2 and 3 with a clear consensus and little doubt, and the vote and trial steps added little.
Dead players still throw and score, so winks have little cost to the victim. Casey's wink in round 3 barely hurt her. Consider limiting scoring for dead players.
